nodes.label:
1. Check Power
is voltage present at the rail?
nodes.title: Check Power
nodes.info: Put a meter on the power rail before anything else. A surprising share of dead circuits are dead because the battery is flat, the USB cable is charge-only, or the rail was never connected. This check costs ten seconds and rules out the most common cause.

nodes.label:
2. Check Continuity
unbroken path, wire by wire?
nodes.title: Check Continuity
nodes.info: With power off, follow the path from supply to component to ground, one wire at a time. Breadboard rows that look connected often are not -- the centre channel splits every row in two, and a jumper seated one hole off is invisible from above.

nodes.label:
3. Check Orientation
polarized parts installed correctly?
nodes.title: Check Orientation
nodes.info: LEDs, electrolytic capacitors, and ICs only work one way round. On an LED the long leg is positive and the flat side of the rim is negative. A backwards LED is not damaged, it is simply silent, which is why this check comes before swapping parts.

nodes.label:
4. Test the Component
swap in a known-good part
nodes.title: Test the Component
nodes.info: Only now is it worth suspecting the part itself. Swap in one you know works. If the circuit springs to life the original was faulty; if it does not, the fault is upstream and you have learned something either way.

nodes.label:
Fault Found
stop and fix it
nodes.title: Fault Found
nodes.info: Stop the checklist as soon as a check fails. The order exists so that the cheapest and most likely causes are eliminated first -- continuing past a found fault just adds variables.
